Agent.text:
I went through the whole app (every screen, the shared logic and the database rules) and fixed the real problems I found. The app builds, all 25 automatic tests pass (6 of them are new), and Craft Anything's own check passes. Nothing is committed or pushed.

**Serious problems fixed:**
- **Deleting a chore erased stars the child had already earned.** If the parent had already used those stars on a reward, the child's balance could even drop below zero. A chore that has history is now archived instead: it disappears from the lists, but the earned stars stay.
- **Deleting a reward gave back the points spent on it.** A reward that has already been redeemed is now hidden from the kids instead of deleted, and the parent gets a message saying why.
- **Point totals would quietly go wrong over time.** The database hands over at most 1,000 records per request, so after about a year of daily chores the oldest ones would stop counting. The app now loads everything, one batch at a time.
- **Two quick taps could spend the same points twice** when redeeming a reward. That's now blocked.
- **A child could mark one daily chore done for many past or future days.** Only the current day, week, month or year is accepted now.

**Smaller fixes:**
- The parent's screens now show the points each child can actually spend, the same number the child sees.
- A double tap or a second parent phone can no longer overwrite an approval that's already been made.
- Saving a chore can no longer leave it with no children assigned if something fails halfway.
- If the parent resets a child's PIN while the child is logged in, the child is now sent back to enter the new PIN instead of getting errors.
- Database error messages, the "page not found" screen and the error screen are now translated into English and German.
- Unsaved typing in Settings is no longer wiped by the automatic refresh.
- Moving between pages is faster.
- Changing the language no longer crashes when the browser blocks saved settings, for example in some private modes.

**One step for you:** the database part of these fixes only takes effect after you apply it with the database update command from your README (`npx supabase db push`). I didn't run it, because it changes your live database. Until then the app works as before, but deleting chores and rewards still wipes their history, and the protection against spending points twice and against marking chores done for other days doesn't apply yet. After applying it, also refresh the app's database descriptions with the command in your project rules (`supabase gen types typescript`); I updated them by hand to match.

**Problems I found but didn't fix (they need a design decision):**
- **Parent mode is only protected inside the browser.** A child who knows how to open the browser's developer tools could switch to parent mode, or approve their own chores. Closing this properly would need a separate parent PIN that the database checks itself.
- **Nothing limits wrong PIN guesses**, so a determined sibling with those tools could eventually find another child's PIN. The database could lock a profile after a few wrong tries.

A good next request would be: "add a parent PIN and lock a profile after too many wrong PIN guesses."

notes: Nothing the check looks at has changed since it last worked, so its results stand.
